extracted.intended_audience: authors, writers, and people interested in beta reading or manuscript feedback
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and role-definitions for using beta readers to test unreleased literary works and provide reader-perspective feedback on manuscript issues. Explains what beta readers do, how they differ from proofreaders/alpha readers/critique partners, and specializations like sensitivity readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot, pacing, and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: This feedback can be used by the writer to fix remaining issues with plot, pacing, and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beta readers identify unresolved narrative problems remaining after revisions; focus is on story-level issues rather than just line edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sounding board for intended intellectual or emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The beta reader also serves as a sounding board to see if the work has the intended intellectual or emotional impact on the target market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript produces the reactions the author intends for the target readership (intellectual engagement, emotional response, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback from the point of view of an average/typical reader
rubrics_metrics.description: A beta reader is a test reader of an unreleased work of writing, typically literature, who gives feedback to the author from the point of view of an average reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reactions and comprehension feedback as a representative reader (not as a writer or specialist); focus on clarity, engagement, and accessibility for the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic scope beyond grammar and spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A proofreader usually only looks at grammar and spelling and is a paid professional, while a beta reader is more holistic in their scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessments of character, plot, pacing, tone, plausibility, and reader experience, not only copyediting-level corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate manuscript stage: post-revision beta reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, a beta reader reviews a draft that has gone through at least one revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beta reading is intended for later-stage drafts (after initial structuring and major revisions); earlier-stage drafts may be more appropriate for alpha readers who review unfinished/unrevised works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast with alpha readers (earlier-stage feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alpha reader reviews a draft that is still without an ending or is completely unrevised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alpha readers for very early development feedback (structure, major gaps); use beta readers once the story is substantially in place to catch remaining issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from critique partners (author-perspective) and proofreaders (copyediting)
rubrics_metrics.description: A critique partner is a trained writer who test reads from the perspective of an author, while a beta reader is a trained reader, test reading from the perspective of a typical reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select critique partners for technical/writerly craft critique; select beta readers to simulate market/reader reactions and detect issues an average reader would notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity readers as specialized beta readers
rubrics_metrics.description: A sensitivity reader is a specific type of beta reader who is from a culture that the author is not familiar with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensitivity readers to evaluate cultural authenticity, representation, and potential harms/insensitivities when the manuscript includes cultures or experiences outside the author's own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of general education and topical awareness in readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Alpha and beta readers must be well educated generally, with a good knowledge of current affairs. This enables them to read works in the current context, with regard to both world affairs and the target market that the work is aimed at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer readers who understand contemporary context and the intended market so their feedback situates the work appropriately; (note: this statement is marked citation needed on the page).
